newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russia regions choose pro-Yeltsin governors.
newsitem.headline: Two Russia regions choose pro-Yeltsin governors.

text.p: Two regional governors originally appointed by President Boris Yeltsin were re-elected in weekend polls, local officials said on Monday.

Voters opted for the status quo by choosing Alexander Filipenko, who won 71.65 percent in the oil-rich district of Khanty-Mansiisk, and Ravil Geniatulin in Chita, near the Chinese border, in first place with 31.75 percent.

But there will be a re-run in two regions where no candidate won enough votes for outright victory on Sunday and a low turnout in the agricultural region of Krasnodar meant the vote there must be held again.
Results from the sixth region were not known.
The regional elections are important on a national level because the governors also become members of the Federation Council upper house of parliament. Voting rules vary from one region to another.
Communists and other conservatives already dominate the lower house of parliament and they are hoping for a strong showing in the regional elections to increase their influence in the upper house.
A second round of voting will be held in Stavropol, in southern Russia, and in Kaluga, southwest of Moscow.

In Krasnodar, former presidential chief-of-staff Nikolai Yegorov, ousted by Yeltsin in July in a purge of Kremlin hardliners, trailed badly in second place but was saved from defeat by the low turnout.
No results were yet available for the remote Anginsky-Buryatsky region, also near the border with China.
